module_title: No Detention Policy Amendments, Non-Academic Duties & NEP 2020 Transition
introduction: Tailored for the highest conceptual tiers of UGC NET and advanced KVS/DSSSB exams, this level dissects the controversial No Detention Policy (and its 2019 amendment), the exact limitations on a teacher's non-academic duties, and how NEP 2020 proposes to overhaul the RTE age brackets.

core_concepts.title: Section 27: Prohibition of Deployment for Non-Educational Purposes
core_concepts.description:
To ensure teaching time is not compromised, Section 27 strictly prohibits the deployment of teachers for non-educational duties. 
However, there are exactly **THREE legal exceptions** where a teacher CAN be deployed:
1. Decennial Population Census.
2. Disaster Relief Duties.
3. Elections (Local authority, State Legislatures, and Parliament). 
*Note: Deploying teachers for polio drops, ration distribution, or generic surveys is illegal under RTE.*

core_concepts.title: The 'No Detention Policy' (NDP) and its Amendment
core_concepts.description:
Original Section 16 (2009): 'No child admitted in a school shall be held back in any class or expelled from school till the completion of elementary education.' (Meaning no student could fail up to Class 8).
Amendment (2019): Due to a massive drop in learning outcomes, the RTE Act was amended. 
- The amendment empowers State Governments to hold a regular examination at the end of Class 5 and Class 8. 
- If a child fails, they are given remedial teaching and a re-examination within 2 months. If they fail again, the State *may* allow schools to hold the child back (detain them).

core_concepts.title: Grievance Redressal: NCPCR & SCPCR
core_concepts.description:
Who monitors the implementation of the RTE Act?
The Act designates the **National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)** at the center and the **State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR)** at the state level to review safeguards, inquire into complaints, and take suo motu cognizance of RTE violations.

core_concepts.title: NEP 2020: The Proposed RTE Expansion
core_concepts.description:
The current RTE Act is structurally limited to the 6-14 age group (Classes 1 to 8). 
NEP 2020 heavily criticizes this limitation. Because NEP 2020 restructures schooling into a 5+3+3+4 model (covering ages 3 to 18), it proposes extending the legal mandate of the RTE Act downwards to include Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE, ages 3-6) and upwards to include Secondary Education (ages 14-18). This would make free and compulsory education a right from **Age 3 to 18**.

important_entities.name: Section 16 vs. Section 17
important_entities.key_fact: No Detention vs. No Corporal Punishment
important_entities.significance: Advanced exams test exact section numbers. Section 16 dealt with the No Detention Policy (now amended). Section 17 deals with the absolute ban on physical punishment and mental harassment.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common exam question: 'Which of the following non-academic duties can a teacher be assigned under RTE?' Options might include 'Pulse Polio duty', 'Mid-day meal cooking', 'Election duty', 'Village survey'. The ONLY correct answer is **Election Duty** (along with Census and Disaster Relief).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember 'CED' to instantly recall the only three non-teaching duties legally allowed for a government teacher under Section 27 of the RTE Act.

exam_strategy_tips: If an advanced question asks about the status of the 'No Detention Policy' today, ensure you select the option that reflects the **2019 Amendment**—states now have the conditional power to detain students in Class 5 and 8 after providing a chance for re-examination.
